title: Nessa and the Lost Bunny
markdown:
Nessa the young witch lived in a little cottage. Its roof was bright blue, like the sky. Smoke puffed out the chimney, smelling yummy like cinnamon and sunshine. Her broomstick leaned by the door, ready for a quick fly. But tonight Nessa was trying something new. She was practising a spell to make her teacups dance. She hummed a happy bubbly tune. Her glasses sat on her nose. She wiggled her fingers. “Dance, little teacups, dance.” One teacup wiggled its handle. Then another did a little shimmy. The teacups twirled and tapped on the table as if they were at a big party.

Suddenly a tiny worried squeak came from just outside her door, a sound so small, like a tiny whisper. Nessa blinked. “That does not sound like a dancing teacup.” Her bright curious eyes got wide with worry. She tiptoed over and peeked out. And there, by her doorstep, was a rabbit. A very fluffy rabbit. Ears soft like dandelion fluff. Tail wagging like a little puffball. He looked a little bit lost. He sighed a tiny sigh.

“Oh, you poor thing.” Her heart felt warm like melted butter. She scooped him up gently. He felt warm and soft, like a little cloud. “Are you lost, little one?” Her voice was as gentle as a butterfly’s wing. The rabbit just nudged her hand with his little pink nose. He did not have a collar, or a little sign. She stroked his soft fur. It felt like velvet. “It is getting late. The Misty Crags can be tricky when it is getting dark. But I cannot leave you here all alone.” She would help this little rabbit find his home.

“Don’t you worry.” He was snuggled in her arms, feeling safe. “We will find your cozy burrow. What is your name?” The rabbit wriggled his nose happily and made a soft little pip-pip sound. “Pipkin.” Nessa giggled. “That is a perfect name for such a sweet little fellow.” And so, with Pipkin tucked safely in her arms, Nessa stepped out into the soft dusky air. The pine trees rustled their needles, making a sound like quiet secrets. The air smelled like damp earth and pinecones.

They walked along a winding path. The moon peeked out from behind a fluffy cloud and cast long gentle shadows that danced like playful sprites. Nessa’s heart felt a little flutter of worry. What if they could not find Pipkin’s home? What if he was very hungry? Just then they saw a warm flickering light ahead. It peeked through the trees like a friendly firefly. It was a small cottage, like Nessa’s own. Outside, a wizard was looking very hard at a very, very big map. This was Wizard Zigzag. He loved maps. He sometimes got them mixed up, just like his long white beard.

“Excuse me, Wizard Zigzag?” Her voice was clear and bright. The wizard jumped a little. He almost tripped over his map, spread out all over his front lawn. “Oh. Hello there, young Nessa. And who is this little fellow you have there?” His eyes twinkled like stars. “This is Pipkin. He seems to be lost. Do you know any rabbit burrows around here? He looks as if he needs to be home for supper.” Wizard Zigzag smoothed out his map. It was so big it covered his garden. “Rabbit burrows, you say? Let me see…” He squinted at a spot that looked like a spilled ink blot. “Ah, yes. According to this map of the Great Cloud Migration… no, wait, that is the map of the Singing Streams. Hmm, perhaps it is this one here, the Guide to Edible Mushrooms? Or this one, the Atlas of Ancient Acorns?”

Nessa smiled kindly. Her brow creased just a little with thought. “Maybe we could look at a simpler map, one that shows paths and homes, Wizard Zigzag? Something a little less twisty?” Wizard Zigzag’s bushy eyebrows shot up. “A simpler map? Oh, my dear child, that is a curious thought. I do have one somewhere.” He rummaged through a pile of scrolls. “Ah, here we are.” He pulled out a map that was much smaller and much, much clearer. “This is the Map of Peaceful Paths. It shows all the lovely little homes where everyone is happy and safe.” Nessa peered at it. It was not as grand or as colourful as the others, but it was much, much clearer. There, near a patch of bright green clover, was a little drawing of a rabbit hole. A tiny wagging tail was peeking out.

“That looks just like Pipkin’s home.” Pipkin wriggled happily in her arms, as if he agreed. Wizard Zigzag beamed. His smile stretched from ear to ear. “Wonderful. Sometimes the simplest maps are the most useful. They do not get all tangled up. And sometimes a wagging tail is the best guide of all. It knows the way home better than any parchment.” He carefully folded the Map of Peaceful Paths and handed it to Nessa. “Thank you so much, Wizard Zigzag.” She held Pipkin close and followed the clear path on the map.

Soon they came to a small welcoming burrow. It glowed softly in the moonlight. It looked cozy and warm. A few other rabbits were peeking out, their noses twitching happily. Pipkin gave a happy pip-pip-pip. He wriggled to be put down. He hopped right towards the burrow. He turned back to give Nessa one last happy wag of his tail before disappearing inside. He was home for supper and a cozy sleep with his family.

Nessa watched him go. Her heart felt as warm as a mug of hot cocoa. As she walked back to her cottage, the moonlight sparkled on the grass like tiny diamonds. The whispering pines seemed to sing a gentle lullaby. At home the teacups had stopped dancing. They waited on the table, still warm from the spell, as if they too had been listening for a wagging tail.
characters: Nessa (young witch who makes teacups dance), Pipkin (a fluffy rabbit with a puffball tail)
author: StoryGen Community
